extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals / communications teams creating press or media kits
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on assembling press kits and media kits (digital or physical) — what to include, formats to use, audience differences, and best practices for making materials journalists, stakeholders, advertisers, and consumers can use. Includes component-level recommendations (company info, press releases, multimedia, fact sheet, contact info) and formatting/maintenance advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press kit audience and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: A press kit is often defined as a collection of materials specifically for journalists, bloggers and media outlets. The goal is to get news coverage for your story by providing all the necessary information about a particular event, product launch or announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press kits are typically concise and focused, providing journalists with everything they need to write a story quickly and accurately. They often support a specific press release and should include the 5 Ws (who, what, when, where, why) along with a few key multimedia pieces to support the story. Example inclusions: the press release announcing the launch; high-quality product photos and specifications; quotes from company executives; background information on product development; relevant industry statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media kit audience and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Media kits are designed for a broader audience that includes not just journalists, but also advertisers, stakeholders and even consumers. The goal is to introduce your business and showcase your brand’s history, key facts and unique selling points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media kits give a fuller picture of your brand’s identity and are used to build long-term relationships and brand awareness. Typical content includes company history and mission statement, key personnel bios, product or service overviews, past media coverage, social media links and posts, audience demographics, case studies or success stories, and recap of major milestones. Media kits can be more extensive than press kits and may be presented as a website or online media room for ongoing access and updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format choice (PDF vs attachments vs online vs physical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Press kits can be shorter and more focused (often formatted as a PDF or a collection of files that can be easily attached to an email). Media kits are usually more extensive and might be formatted as a website or online media room. Physical copies are less common but useful for in-person events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose format based on audience and use case. PDFs work for single-document overviews (use bookmarks/TOC). Attachments give flexibility to send only needed pieces (use consistent naming and a readme). Online media rooms provide 24/7 access and interactive elements and are easy to update. Physical kits (high-quality folders, business cards, branded items) are helpful at trade shows and in-person events.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF formatting guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: A single PDF document can be an effective and simple way to format your kit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bookmarks or a clickable table of contents for easy navigation and include links to external resources like press releases, social media and downloadable assets. PDFs maintain formatting across devices and are universally accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment-based kits and naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: If you want more flexibility, create separate files for different elements of your kit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent naming conventions for easy identification and provide a “readme” file explaining what each attachment contains. Compress large high-resolution files for easier sharing. This approach makes it easier to update individual elements and to send only what’s needed to a particular recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online media room best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: An online media room is a live version of your press or media kit that provides 24/7 access to your information and can include interactive elements like video players or live social media feeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a dedicated section on your website, organize content into clear categories, and regularly update it with fresh content (like a blog, but for news). Use it to host downloadable assets, press releases, fact sheets, and multimedia; ensure it’s easy to navigate and searchable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical press kit presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical press kits are still useful for in-person events and should be well-presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use high-quality folders or presentation materials and include business cards and other branded items. Physical kits stand out at trade shows or media events by providing a tangible representation of your brand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update cadence / timeline differences
rubrics_metrics.description: A press kit can be a more timely release that coincides with specific events or announcements; press kits are updated frequently to stay current. Media kits are sometimes a separate item that focuses on the organization’s long-term strategy and are only updated periodically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because digital tools make updating easier, organizations often combine press and media kits; still, plan updates according to whether the kit serves immediate news needs or long-term brand positioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include the 5 Ws for news-focused content
rubrics_metrics.description: Press kits should include the 5 Ws (who, what, when, where, why).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing these core facts helps journalists write a story quickly. Combine the 5 Ws with a press release and supporting multimedia to make it easy to produce coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company information section requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Your company information section should go beyond the basic press release boilerplate and help journalists and stakeholders understand what really sets you apart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a list of awards and recognitions, company values and mission statement, leadership bios with professional headshots and sound bites, stats about key audience demographics, other strengths, and multiple high-resolution versions of your approved logo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press releases to include
rubrics_metrics.description: If you’re sending the kit to accompany a specific press release, you don’t need to include other releases. For a general information kit or online posting, include three to five recent, newsworthy press releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a mix of release types (product launches, company news, thought leadership) and include links to the releases to demonstrate that your company is active and newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Downloadable multimedia assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a section for multimedia assets, like images, video and audio, to make it easy for journalists to create visually appealing stories about your brand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide high-resolution infographics, product images from multiple angles, team photos and headshots, B-roll video footage, and audio clips from leadership and industry experts. The more comprehensive and high-quality your multimedia, the easier you make it for others to tell your story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact sheet content and format
rubrics_metrics.description: A well-crafted fact sheet provides a quick reference and is a must-have for journalists on tight deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a one-page document or chart that summarizes key information about what your company does, pricing information, ways to purchase, distributor information, competitor comparisons and technical specifications. Treat it as a cheat sheet about your business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media section expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The social media section should do more than just list your accounts; it should showcase your brand’s online personality and provide ready-made content for stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include embedded examples of popular posts and highlights from reviewers or influencers who have mentioned your brand. Add key metrics about social media following and engagement, and provide ready-made quotes or content snippets journalists can reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear and accessible contact information is essential and should be part of any kit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the name and role of the primary media contact, a direct phone number (not just a general company line), and an email address. Mention best times to reach out and provide an alternative contact. Making it easy to get in touch increases the chances of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor kit content to industry and audience
rubrics_metrics.description: What to include in a media kit can vary — make sure you tailor the content to your industry and target audience for maximum impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider which assets and metrics are most persuasive for journalists, advertisers, investors, or consumers, and emphasize those elements (e.g., case studies for B2B, influencer mentions for consumer brands).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include executive quotes and sound bites
rubrics_metrics.description: Press kits often include quotes from company executives to provide commentary and context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concise, media-ready quotes and sound bites that journalists can use directly in coverage; include attribution and, where appropriate, brief bios to establish authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate newsworthiness and activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Including recent press releases, past media coverage, and case studies shows that your company is active and newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a mix of materials (product launches, company news, thought leadership) and links to coverage to help journalists assess relevance quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make materials easy to use and download
rubrics_metrics.description: The kit should make it easy for others to tell your story by providing ready-to-use materials and clear access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer downloadable high-resolution assets, compressed files for sharing when necessary, clear filenames/descriptions, and a readme or guidance that tells journalists what each file is and how it can be used.
